questiontext.text: When a polynomial is stored as a linked list of terms, what does each term node hold?

feedback.text: Correct — one node per term, storing (coefficient, exponent).
Without the exponent you cannot tell which power the term is.
The coefficient is needed to know the term's magnitude.

answer.text: the entire polynomial as a string

feedback.text: Each node holds a single term, not the whole polynomial.

generalfeedback.text: A term node is (coefficient, exponent) plus a link to the next term.

questiontext.text: In the standard representation, the term nodes are kept sorted by...

feedback.text: Correct — highest power first makes merging a single pass.
Coefficients do not define term order.
Unordered terms would make addition harder.
These are single-variable polynomials ordered by exponent.

generalfeedback.text: Sorting by descending exponent lets addition merge the two lists in one linear pass.

questiontext.text: During addition, when two terms have the equal exponent you...

answer.text: sum their coefficients into one term

feedback.text: Correct — like powers combine.
Exponents are matched, not added.
Terms of the same power must be combined.
Addition sums coefficients; it does not multiply them.

generalfeedback.text: Terms with the same exponent are combined by adding coefficients; the exponent stays the same.

questiontext.text: If two combined terms have coefficients that sum to zero, the result term is...

feedback.text: Correct — a zero coefficient contributes nothing and is omitted.
Storing explicit zeros wastes space and is avoided.
It simply vanishes; no constant is introduced.
The term is removed, not re-exponented.

generalfeedback.text: When coefficients cancel to zero, the term is dropped so the list holds only nonzero terms.

questiontext.text: Because both lists are sorted by exponent, addition can merge them in a single linear pass.

feedback.text: Correct — a merge like two sorted lists, comparing leading exponents.
Sorted order makes a single linear merge possible.

questiontext.text: To add two polynomials, you add the exponents of matching terms.

feedback.text: You sum coefficients of equal-exponent terms; exponents are unchanged.
Correct — matching means equal exponents; you add coefficients.

questiontext.text: The terms of the polynomial list are kept sorted by their ______, the power to which the variable is raised.

feedback.text: Correct.
Correct.

questiontext.text: Which statements about linked-list polynomial addition are true? (select all that apply)

answer.text: Each node stores a coefficient and an exponent

feedback.text: Yes — one term per node.

answer.text: Terms with equal exponents have their coefficients summed

feedback.text: Yes — like powers combine.

answer.text: Terms are stored in ascending exponent order

feedback.text: No — they are kept in descending exponent order.

answer.text: Terms whose coefficients sum to zero are kept in the result

feedback.text: No — zero terms are dropped.

generalfeedback.text: Nodes are (coeff, exp) in descending exponent order; equal exponents merge by summing coefficients; zero results are dropped.
